fields.meta_title: Dynamic Landing Pages by Ad and Audience | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build dynamic landing pages that swap the headline by ad keyword, audience tag or CRM record, and save which version each visitor saw.
fields.h1: Build Dynamic Landing Pages That Match Every Ad and Audience
fields.hero_description: Build dynamic landing pages that swap the headline for each ad or audience and save every visit to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: How One Page Becomes Many Versions
fields.features_subheading: One URL, one build. The link a visitor clicks picks the headline and offer they read, and each visit is logged against that version.
fields.feature_1:
Versions described in plain English

Describe each version of the page and the link tag that picks it. Emergent builds the page, the swap rules, and the visits table from that prompt, and edits any rule when you ask.
fields.feature_2:
The ad keyword, placed in the headline

Google Ads can pass the keyword that matched a search into your final URL. The page reads it from the link and places it in the headline and on the quote button above the fold.
fields.feature_3:
A default for blank or unknown tags

A link with no tag, or a tag the page has no rule for, gets the default headline you wrote. Visitors who arrive from a bookmark or a forwarded link still read a complete page.
fields.feature_4:
CRM fields filled in through the API

Put a contact's record ID in the email link. The page then looks up the company name and account owner in HubSpot, or any CRM with an API, and writes them into the copy.
fields.feature_5:
Every visit saved with its version

Each visit lands as a row in a database you own, with the version shown, the tag that chose it, and whether the visitor converted. A live dashboard counts signups per version.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, or the code in GitHub

Publish on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code, swap rules and all, to your GitHub repository and keep building there.

fields.usecase_heading: Dynamic Landing Page Examples by Signal
fields.tab_content_1:
A click from the piano movers ad gets a piano headline

Fenwood Movers in Columbus runs one ad group per service, and Google Ads' {keyword} parameter adds the matched keyword to each final URL. The piano movers ad opens on "Piano moving in Columbus, padded and strapped." This week it sent 148 visitors, and 23 asked for a quote, each saved with its keyword.
fields.tab_content_2:
With the vet tag, a vet headline and quote

Cinderbay's LinkedIn ads for dental offices and vet clinics point to one demo page, each ad link carrying an industry tag. The tag picks the headline and quote, and vet visitors read "Fewer missed vet appointments." This month brought 41 demo requests under the dental tag, 29 under the vet tag, and 6 untagged.
fields.tab_content_3:
Delmar Freight's page opens with its own name and fleet

Kestovar emails 40 target accounts a link carrying each contact's HubSpot record ID. The page reads the company name and fleet size through HubSpot's API and opens on "Fuel reports for Delmar Freight's 220 trucks." When that contact books a call, Ada Quarrier, who owns the account, gets a Slack message.
fields.tab_content_4:
Signups by source put the newsletter version first

Bramblecut Coffee tags the links to its subscription page by source, and every visit is saved with the version it saw. On the live dashboard, the newsletter version has 87 signups from 960 visits. The Instagram version, written for first-time buyers, has 74 from 1,840 visits.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Dynamic Landing Pages
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to dynamic landing pages that swap copy by link tag and report each version's results, then build them with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what each incoming link can carry: the ad keyword, a campaign tag, a CRM record ID, or the traffic source. Personalize on signals you put in the link yourself. A guess about the visitor is harder to test and easier to get wrong.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Start with the headline. It is the first line a visitor reads and the line the ad or email promised. Add a second swap, such as the customer quote or the offer, once the headline versions have enough visits to compare.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the page an untagged visitor sees before any variant. Make it complete on its own, because bookmarks, forwarded emails, and search visitors all land there. Every tagged version is then a small edit to this page, not a separate build.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For search ads, add Google Ads' {keyword} parameter to the final URL and set the headline from it. Keep an approved headline for each keyword you bid on, so a misspelled or unexpected match shows the default instead of odd text.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Google defines cloaking as presenting different content to users and search engines to manipulate rankings and mislead users. Serve search engines the same default page an untagged visitor gets, and keep tagged versions for ad and email traffic.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Log the version behind each signup
fields.howto_step_6_des: Store which version each visitor saw next to the signup or request it led to. Without that pairing, the dashboard shows total signups but not which headline earned them. Compare versions only after each has a few hundred visits.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the versions, the link tags, and the default in one prompt. Emergent builds the page and its rules, then edits a headline or adds a version when you ask. Click every tagged link yourself before the campaign starts.
fields.hero_prompt: Build dynamic landing pages for my moving company that change the headline to match the keyword in each ad click.

faq_plan.q: How do I create dynamic landing pages?

plan.angle: The top 10 splits between personalization vendors selling a script that sits on an existing page (Personyze, Digioh, Dynamic Yield), definition and example posts (Unbounce, Wix), HubSpot's docs on data-driven pages and a Reddit thread asking how to build one for a sofa store's ads. None shows the build: which link tag picks which version, what the visitor sees when the tag is blank, and how you learn which version earned signups. This page shows four working dynamic pages by the signal that drives the swap (the ad keyword, an audience tag, a CRM record, the traffic source), each with the visits saved per version, and the FAQ covers the definition, building one, keyword insertion, fallbacks, SEO and measurement.
tab_stories: Fenwood Movers in Columbus passes the matched keyword into each ad's final URL, so the piano movers ad opens on a piano headline; that keyword sent 148 visitors this week and 23 asked for a quote, each saved with the keyword.

Cinderbay, booking software for clinics, sends LinkedIn ads for dental, vet and physio clinics to one page whose industry tag picks the headline and customer quote, and demo requests are counted per tag: 41 dental, 29 vet, 17 physio.

Kestovar, fleet analytics, emails 40 target accounts a link with each contact's HubSpot record ID; the page fills in Delmar Freight's name and its 220 trucks, and when the contact books a call, account owner Ada Quarrier gets a Slack message.

Bramblecut Coffee tags its subscription page links by source, every visit is saved with the version it saw, and a live dashboard shows the newsletter version converting at 9.1% against 7.6% for the podcast and 4.0% for Instagram.
